1. The function has a local maximum at \(x=-2\).
2. The function has a local minimum at \(x=2\).
3. Between these two turning points, the graph is continuously going downward, so \(f(x)\) is strictly decreasing there.
4. To the left of \(-2\) it is increasing, and to the right of \(2\) it is increasing again.

Thus the largest interval on which \(f(x)\) is strictly decreasing is

\[
\boxed{[-2,\;2]}
\]

(Equivalently, the open interval is \((-2,2)\), but the requested \([a,b]\) format includes the endpoints.)
